title: Arise My Soul, My Joyful Powers
description: Arise My Soul, My Joyful Powers in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 82, headed “Redemption and protection from spiritual enemies”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-rise my soul, my joy-ful powers, And tri-umph in my God, A-wake, my voice, and loud pro-claim His glo-rious grace a-broad.

lines: Arise my soul, my joyful powers,
Awake, my voice, and loud proclaim
He rais'd me from the deeps of sin,
And fix'd my standing more secure
And on the rock of ages set
The city of my bless'd abode
Satan may vent his sharpest spite,
Arise, my soul, awake, my voice,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
